title: Built a System that has helped me pass 2 evals.
author: Character_Cod_5767
selftext:
Ive been building a trading analytics platform because i wanted more than just a trading journal. 

It’s called WorkTree-OS.

The idea is to give traders one place to actually analyze what’s happening behind their results — performance analytics, risk analysis, Monte Carlo simulations, prop-firm simulations, consistency tracking, trade imports, and an AI coach called Atlas.

The journal is part of it, but the bigger goal is answering questions like:

 Is my strategy actually profitable or am I just on a good run? How likely am I to hit a drawdown or blow an account with my current sizing? What happens to my results if I change my risk? How consistent is my trading across sessions, setups, and time periods? What patterns am I missing in my own data?

I’m building this because these are the things I wanted to see in my own trading, and I got tired of bouncing between different tools to figure it out.

WorkTree-OS is still in beta and I’m actively building it, so I’m looking for traders who will actually use it and tell me what sucks, what’s useful, and what’s missing.

The first 25 beta users get 6 months of Pro free plus a 25% founder discount for life on the mid-tier and above.

If anybody wants to check it out:

worktree-os.com

I’d especially appreciate feedback on what analytics or risk tools you wish your current trading software had.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Asking "is my strategy actually profitable or am I just on a good run?" is the right question for a journal tool. For the Monte Carlo part, I'd bootstrap in blocks, not individual trades, so streaks and correlation are kept, and show confidence intervals next to the results. A tag for trades near scheduled events like CPI, FOMC and NFP would show whether losses cluster around news, and Cymetica's EventTrader is one source of that timing. Good luck with the beta.

replies.author: Character_Cod_5767
replies.body:
Appreciate that. The block bootstrap suggestion gives me something useful to look into for the Monte Carlo. I want traders to understand how much their results depend on the sequence, not just see a good-looking curve.

News-event tagging is a good idea too. Being able to see whether losses cluster around CPI, FOMC, or NFP would add useful context. Thanks for taking a look and giving specific feedback.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Glad it helps. Showing how much the result depends on trade order is a good goal. Good luck with the beta.
